title: CRLR/79/2007 of DAYA SHANKAR Vs STATE AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.79 of 2007

Daya Shankar ÖÖÖ. Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttaranchal & others ..Ö. Respondents
Dated: May 31, 2013
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 This Court has rendered hearing to Mr. B.S.
Adhikari, Advocate for the revisionist and Mr. Amit Kapri,
Brief Holder for the State. None has turned up on behalf
of private opposite parties though notices upon them
have sufficiently been served and name of their counsel
also appears in the list.
 This revision is against the judgment and order
dated 2.12.2006 passed by the Additional Family Judge,
Rishikesh, Dehradun, whereby the wife of revisionist
Smt. Shalini Rajput and her daughter Km. Abhilasha
were granted Rs.3,500/- and Rs.1,500/- per month
respectively (in total Rs.5,000/- per month) as
maintenance allowance from the date of moving such
application i.e. 22.7.2004.
 Learned counsel has argued that during the course
of contesting the maintenance petition, revisionist was
continuously paying interim maintenance @Rs.1,500/-
per month to the private respondents, and it has further
been argued that as per the salary receipt, which adverts
the monthly salary of Rs.17,575/-, the amount, so
granted to the private respondents, is exorbitant. This

2
Court is not satisfied with the said contention and feels
that the revisionist, who has been shown as Lieutenant
in the year 2005 in the salary-slip, must have been at the
rank of Lieutenant Colonel by now. Besides, considering
the revisionist either as Lieutenant or Captain in the
Army, his wife and child are supposed to be of the
equivalent status as that of revisionist. So, awarding of
maintenance @Rs.5,000/- per mensem was not
exorbitant at all, and it is of no affect that she was being
awarded a meager subsistence allowance to the tune of
Rs.1,500/- per month during the course of pendency of
litigation. The Court feels that the revision is bereft of
any merit and liable to be dismissed. Revision is
accordingly, dismissed. However, the amount, already
paid by the revisionist to this wife and child, shall be
adjusted while reckoning the amount of arrears. It will
be the discretion of the Drawing & Disbursing Officer of
the revisionist to make the amount recoverable from the
revisionist, in reasonable installments, so that to leave a
sufficient amount with him for his subsistence.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
31.05.2013
Rajeev Dang
